text:
kevin: ran a quick microbench on paged+packed KV with flash-hybrid and fused-flash variants. seeing 12-18% regression for seq >= 2048 on A100 when dtype=bfloat16. :thinking:
rita: hm, is that on the fused kernel or the paged fallback?
maria: looks like fused-flash for short sequences, but after we cross page boundary the runtime picks paged+flash-hybrid and perf drops. i can paste the profile.
kevin: here's the core output from `nvprof` and our tracer (trimmed):
```
chrtracer: kernel=flash_fused_v2, seq=1024, qps=540
chrtracer: kernel=flash_hybrid_paged, seq=2048, qps=440  # big drop
nvprof: cudaMemcpy H2D 3.2ms, launch flash_hybrid_paged 1.1ms, memset 0.2ms
```
alex: interesting that memcpy spikes. are we packing KV interleaved? or separate K/V pages?
kevin: interleaved pack (K0 V0 K1 V1 ...). tried separate layout once but didnt re-run the full bench.
rita: interleaved helps small-batch coalescing but can cause unaligned accesses when dtype=bf16 -> 3/4 word boundaries? alignment matters.
maria: right — on A100 L2/cache width, we should align to 128 bytes for best coalescing on fused kernels. if stride isn't a multiple of 128 bytes we get partial cache lines and higher load latency.
kevin: i instrumented memory addresses; lots of loads crossing 128B boundaries at page offsets. stride pattern caused by interleaving + 96-byte per-token footprint (bfloat16).
rita: try 128-byte padding between KV entries or switch to separate arrays: keys contiguous, values contiguous. separate also lets us use vectorized loads for Q*K dot prods in fused kernels.
maria: also keep an eye on warp-level bank conflicts with interleave. fused flash assumes packed contiguous QKV layout per head. paged kernels are more tolerant but memcpy cost kills you.
alex: a few practical experiments to run: 
- bench interleaved vs separate with seq in [512,1024,2048,4096]
- run dtype=float16 vs bfloat16 for both layouts
- test alignment paddings of 64/128/256 bytes
- measure host->device memcpy times and kernel launch times separately
kevin: i'll run those overnight and feed results to perf-bot. starting with a matrix: batch=1, heads=32, head_dim=64, model=30B config.
perf-bot: automated-profile: 1966667777-run1: interleaved-bf16-seq2048: avg_tok_ms=0.73, memcpy=3.1ms, kernel=1.2ms. interleaved-fp16-seq2048: avg_tok_ms=0.61, memcpy=0.9ms, kernel=0.95ms. separate-bf16-seq2048: avg_tok_ms=0.58, memcpy=0.8ms, kernel=0.94ms.
rita: perf-bot numbers already show separate layout recovers a lot. memcpy difference suggests we were copying more (or less contiguous) memory in interleaved case.
maria: so hypothesis: interleaved+bf16 leads to misaligned 128B boundaries -> more H2D fragmentation + kernel reads scattered -> paged kernel suffers. separate layout + 128B pad removes boundary crossing.
alex: also consider kernel selection heuristic: if seq>threshold (2048), prefer fused-hybrid but only when layout is contiguous or when dtype==fp16. otherwise prefer fused-flash or fallback to fused that expects separate layout.
kevin: can we add a quick runtime check: compute worst-case stride alignment for a request and attach a hint to kernel selector? cheap: compute (base_addr % 128) and (stride_bytes % 128).
rita: yes. add a fast path: if (stride % 128 == 0 && dtype==fp16) => allow flash_fused_v2; else prefer flash_hybrid_paged or separate-layout-optimized kernel.
maria: also worth adding an ABI compat check in model-loader to emit a layout-compatibility bit so Dedicated/private customers can pin layout choices.
kevin: will prototype the selector change in the runtime. patch plan: 
- metric: token ms delta and memcpy time logged per request
- selector: alignment check + dtype check + seq threshold tunable
- rollout: canary on 10% traffic with telemetry aggregated to perf dashboards
alex: sounds good. small note: for safety, fall back to current behavior if selector heuristic not present. add opt-in env var `RW_KV_LAYOUT_HINT=true` for tests.
maria: can we also add unit microbench for stride patterns into the CI perf suite? tiny synthetic that checks 64/96/128/256 paddings.
kevin: yes. i'll add that to eng-runtime/perf-tests.
rita: great. action items: kevin runs the experiment set and posts detailed csv; kevin + maria implement selector heuristic; alex wires telemetry; perf-bot to aggregate. :thumbsup:
kevin: starting runs now. will post CSV link when ready. :eyes:
